decisions.thought: Dragonite is the safest response: it resists Ogerpon-Wellspring’s Grass STAB, is neutral to Water, and Multiscale prevents an immediate knockout. Kingambit risks taking heavy damage before Iron Head can make progress, while Dragonite can preserve momentum and threaten Dragon Dance or Earthquake.

Ogerpon-Wellspring naturally outspeeds Kingambit. Ivy Cudgel (Water-type STAB on Wellspring forme) deals strong neutral damage without making contact, easily 2HKOing standard Kingambit while punishing switch-ins.

Dragonite comfortably survives Ivy Cudgel thanks to its Grass resistance and Multiscale. Dragon Dance exploits the favorable matchup, outspeeds Ogerpon afterward, and threatens strong follow-up damage without wasting Terastallization.

Dragonite's Multiscale is already broken (at 87% HP). Ogerpon-Wellspring naturally outspeeds non-boosted Dragonite and carries Play Rough, which targets Dragonite's 2x Fairy weakness and guarantees an immediate knockout.

Dragonite is at 13% HP and +1 Speed/+1 Attack. Dragonite may click Extreme Speed, but +1 Dragonite Extreme Speed cannot OHKO a full HP Ogerpon-Wellspring. Ivy Cudgel has 100% accuracy and easily picks up the remaining 13% HP.
Tera Normal Extreme Speed uses Dragonite’s +1 Attack and priority to strike before Ogerpon. The boosted STAB damage should KO Wellspring Ogerpon from full, avoiding the otherwise fatal Ivy Cudgel.

Gholdengo is the safest entry: it outspeeds Ogerpon, resists the displayed Grass-type Ivy Cudgel, and threatens an immediate KO with Make It Rain. It also avoids the Fairy weakness that makes Dragapult and Great Tusk risky.
Make It Rain is super effective against Ogerpon-Wellspring and easily secures the knockout from 4% HP, while also being the strongest option if the opponent switches.
Opposing Gholdengo is at 31% HP at -1 Special Attack. Choice Scarf Gholdengo easily outspeeds and cleans it up with Shadow Ball, maintaining huge offensive momentum without risk.

Ting-Lu is the safest switch: its Dark typing makes it immune to opposing Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball, while Vessel of Ruin and its massive special bulk mitigate Make It Rain. It then threatens an immediate Earthquake, unlike the vulnerable low-HP Gholdengo.
Our Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds opposing Gholdengo (which cannot Terastallize as Dragonite already Tera'd). Shadow Ball easily finishes off the opposing Gholdengo at 31% HP.

Earthquake is the decisive play: Ting-Lu outspeeds this Gholdengo and Ground STAB is super effective, likely scoring an immediate knockout from full. Switching gives Gholdengo a chance to exploit the momentum, while Ruination is unnecessary unless an Air Balloon is present.

Gholdengo is locked into Shadow Ball against Ting-Lu, which resists it and threatens Gholdengo heavily. Iron Valiant hard-counters Ting-Lu and Kingambit with STAB Close Combat and Moonblast, gaining Booster Energy immediately. Switching to Iron Valiant is the optimal play.

Earthquake is the decisive play: Iron Valiant is already near its knockout threshold, and Ting-Lu survives likely coverage comfortably. Ruination is unreliable due to its 90% accuracy and only creates a two-hit sequence, while switching forfeits pressure.

Iron Valiant outspeeds Ting-Lu. Close Combat targets Ting-Lu's physical defense without suffering from Vessel of Ruin's 25% special attack reduction, dealing substantial damage and also threatening Kingambit if it switches in.

decisions.thought: Stealth Rock is the strongest immediate play: Ribombee is unlikely to threaten a knockout from this healthy Ting-Lu, and hazards heavily punish the opponent’s remaining switches. Setting rocks now also supports Dragapult and Kingambit’s endgame while avoiding the imperfect accuracy of Ruination.

Ribombee is at full HP with Focus Sash intact and naturally resists Ground-type Earthquake from Ting-Lu. Setting Sticky Web now provides critical speed control against the remaining opposing threats (Kingambit, etc.), enabling our team to clean up smoothly.

Earthquake is the decisive play: it heavily damages or likely knocks out frail Ribombee, while also punishing any non-Gholdengo switch. Ting-Lu should capitalize on the immediate offensive pressure rather than spend another turn setting hazards.

Sticky Web is already set on the opponent's side. Ribombee heavily threatens Ting-Lu with STAB super-effective Moonblast, and Ribombee is faster with Focus Sash intact. Clicking Moonblast applies maximum pressure without risking unnecessary switch damage.

Earthquake is the decisive play: it threatens to KO Ribombee and also heavily punishes a switch to the revealed Gholdengo. Ting-Lu is low, but preserving momentum is more valuable than switching into Sticky Web and Stealth Rock while giving the opponent another free turn.

Opponent's Ting-Lu is at 35% HP and cannot Terastallize. Sticky Web is already up on the opponent's side. Ribombee's Moonblast hits Ting-Lu for super effective STAB damage, easily picking up the knockout from this range.
Kingambit is the safest entry: it resists Ribombee’s Moonblast and threatens an immediate KO with super-effective Iron Head, while Sticky Web makes the faster options unreliable.

Ironhead is the decisive KO: it is super effective against Ribombee and comfortably finishes its 63% HP, whereas Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch are resisted by Fairy. Kingambit can survive a likely Moonblast, so attack immediately rather than set up.

decisions.thought: Ironhead is the decisive play: it hits Samurott-H neutrally and exploits its poor physical Defense, while Kowtow Cleave is resisted. At 88% HP, Ironhead has the best chance to secure the knockout and prevents Samurott from setting hazards or attacking.

Opponent's Kingambit has already Terastallized (Dragonite used Tera Normal earlier, opponent has used Tera).
Our active is Samurott-Hisui (faster, especially with opponent Kingambit at -1 Speed from Sticky Web).
Samurott-Hisui has Sharpness boosting Razor Shell (75 BP * 1.5 Sharpness * 1.5 STAB = 168.75 effective BP) and a 50% chance to drop Defense.
Razor Shell easily deals massive neutral damage to Kingambit, likely 2HKOing or setting up for our Kingambit/Gholdengo in the back. Knock Off removes item (likely Leftovers, Lum, or Air Balloon), but Razor Shell deals significantly more immediate damage boosted by Sharpness.
Razor Shell is the most reliable high-damage play here.
Kowtow Cleave is the strongest reliable option and should KO the weakened Samurott-Hisui. It also heavily punishes a switch to the opposing Gholdengo, while Sucker Punch is weaker and conditional.

Opposing Kingambit is at 71% HP, at -1 Def and -1 Spe, and cannot Terastallize (Dragonite already Terastallized).
Our Samurott-Hisui is faster (295 Spe vs -1 Kingambit).
Razor Shell is boosted by Sharpness (1.5x) + STAB (1.5x), effectively 168.75 BP against a -1 Def Kingambit.
Damage calculation:
Razor Shell at -1 Def Kingambit: 252+ Atk Sharpness Samurott-H Razor Shell vs. -1 0 HP / 0 Def Kingambit deals roughly 75-90% HP, which easily guarantees a KO on a 71% Kingambit.
Furthermore, Razor Shell ignores potential Sucker Punch mindgames if it just takes the hit (Kingambit Sucker Punch might do ~60-70%, but our Samurott resists Dark; Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head won't KO from 53.3% if resisted or if Sucker Punch is used, Samurott resists Dark and Steel).
Actually, Samurott-H resists Dark and Steel. Sucker Punch from Kingambit vs Water/Dark does very little.
Razor Shell is the most reliable, high-damage move to KO Kingambit directly.

Samurott-Hisui fainted. We need to choose our switch-in. Kingambit receives the maximum Supreme Overlord boost (5 fainted allies, +50% attack boost) and has Sucker Punch + Kowtow Cleave to easily clean up the opponent's chipped Kingambit (19% HP, -2 Def) and Gholdengo (31% HP). Sending in Kingambit secures the endgame.

Great Tusk is the decisive switch: it comfortably handles opposing Kingambit and threatens an immediate KO with Close Combat, while preserving our weakened Kingambit is less valuable. Even if the opponent attacks or uses Swords Dance, Tusk remains the best counterplay.
Opposing Kingambit is at 19% HP, -1 Speed, and -2 Defense. Our Kingambit easily outspeeds and Kowtow Cleave is a guaranteed knockout that bypasses any Sucker Punch mindgames.
Close Combat is decisively strongest: it receives STAB and hits Kingambit for 4× super-effective damage, comfortably securing the knockout before its slower Kingambit can respond.

Great Tusk is lowered to -1 Speed by Sticky Web. Kingambit with 4 Supreme Overlord boosts hits extremely hard. Terastallizing eliminates Kingambit's 4x Fighting and 2x Ground weaknesses, allowing it to easily survive Great Tusk's STAB attack and retaliate with massive damage via Kowtow Cleave to break through the opponent's remaining team.

Close Combat cleanly KOs the 20% Tera Fire Kingambit and avoids the possibility of an Air Balloon invalidating Headlong Rush. Great Tusk must attack now before being picked off, and Fighting is super effective against Fire.
Great Tusk is at 19% HP with -1 Defense. Kingambit has Supreme Overlord boost active from 4 fainted teammates. Sucker Punch is guaranteed to pick up the knockout before Great Tusk can attack.

Dragapult is the safest endgame entry: it is at full health, remains faster than Tera Fire Kingambit despite Sticky Web, and threatens an immediate KO with Specs Shadow Ball while preserving the nearly fainted Kingambit as a potential priority fallback.

Shadow Ball is guaranteed to move first and cleanly KO the weakened Tera Fire Kingambit without risking Draco Meteor’s accuracy or Special Attack drop. It also avoids giving Sucker Punch value if the knockout occurs.

Kingambit has 4 Supreme Overlord boosts (+40% attack). Sucker Punch against Ghost-type Dragapult is an easy 100% OHKO. Kingambit holds Lum Berry, so even if Dragapult attempts Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave, it is protected, and Sucker Punch bypasses Speed tiers to eliminate the biggest threat immediately.

Switch Kingambit in: it resists the opponent’s revealed Dark attacks, while Gholdengo is vulnerable to Kowtow Cleave and likely cannot survive. Kingambit can threaten an immediate boosted Sucker Punch against the weakened opposing Kingambit.

Kowtow Cleave is the safest knockout: opposing Fire-terastallized Kingambit is at only 20%, while Sucker Punch is less reliable if it uses a non-attacking move. Do not switch, since Gholdengo cannot afford the opposing Kingambit’s Dark attacks.

Opponent Kingambit is at 19% HP and -1 Speed from Sticky Web. My Kingambit easily outspeeds it (199 Speed).
If the opponent attempts Sucker Punch, the priority bracket ties and speed determines turn order—my Kingambit goes first due to higher base speed and their -1 Speed drop.
Sucker Punch guarantees moving before any attack and secures the KO on opposing Kingambit.
Gholdengo is the only surviving Pokémon and the sole legal action. It must switch in against the opposing Fire-terastallized Kingambit.

Shadow Ball is the safest guaranteed KO: it hits Tera Fire Kingambit neutrally and easily exceeds its remaining 20% HP. Focus Blast is unnecessary and risks a miss, while Make It Rain is resisted. Gholdengo outspeeds standard Kingambit even after Sticky Web.

Opponent has only Gholdengo remaining at 31% HP.
Kingambit has 4 Supreme Overlord boosts. Sucker Punch (+1 priority) guarantees the knockout before Gholdengo can move, securing the win immediately.
